transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I’ve been feeling kind of foggy in my head lately. I’m making little mistakes in my client notes at work and forgetting what I was about to do, which really isn’t like me.
How long have you been feeling this foggy in your head?
It’s been about a month now. The foggy feeling, and feeling low and guilty, it’s just kind of been hanging over me that whole time.
Can you tell me more about feeling low that you mentioned, is that something you've been experiencing every day?
Yeah, pretty much every day lately. I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I can still get through my shift and talk to people, but inside I just feel sad and kind of flat.
Have you experienced any loss of interest in activities you normally enjoy?
I’m not sure I’d call it a loss of interest exactly. I still do things when I need to, but I guess I haven’t really felt excited about much lately. It’s more like I’m just going through the motions.
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide over the past month?

I haven’t made any plans to hurt myself or anything like that. But… yeah, there have been some mornings where I think maybe it wouldn’t be the worst thing if I just didn’t wake up. That scares me to admit.
Would you say that this heavy, empty feeling in your chest is mild, moderate, or severe most of the time?
Most of the time I’d say it’s mild. It’s there when I wake up, that heavy, empty feeling, but I can still get through work and talk to people. Inside I just feel sad and kind of flat.
Have you noticed any problems with your relationships at work or with friends and family since you started feeling this way?

Yeah, a little. At work I’ve had to ask coworkers to double-check my client documentation because I’m missing details more than usual. And at home, my wife has been handling some of the bills and scheduling, just because I’m not as reliable with that stuff right now.
Would you say that your overall mood is moderately depressed or just mildly depressed most of the time?
I’d call it mild most of the time. I wake up with that heavy, empty feeling, but I can still get through my shift and talk to people. Inside, though, I feel sad and kind of flat.
Are there any activities that you used to do daily or almost daily that you've stopped doing or are doing less often since you started feeling this way?
I’m not sure there’s anything I’ve completely stopped doing daily. I guess I’m doing some things a little less, but nothing really stands out as a big change.
Have you had to cut back on any of your work or social activities because of these feelings?

A little, yeah. I haven’t really stopped working or seeing people completely, but I’ve had to lean on others more. At work I’m asking coworkers to double-check my client notes because I’m missing details, and at home my wife has taken over some bills and scheduling since I’m not as reliable with that right now.
Are you having difficulty performing your daily tasks because of these feelings of sadness and foggy head?

Yeah, some. I’m still getting through the day, but I’m not as sharp with details. At work I’ve had to ask coworkers to double-check my client notes, and at home my wife has been handling more of the bills and scheduling because I’ve been missing things.
Have there been any days over the past month where you felt more than just mildly depressed?

Yeah, there have been days like that. I can still get up and go to work and talk to people, but I’ll wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It’s not just a little down—it’s more like I feel sad and flat inside.
On those days when you feel more than mildly depressed, would you describe your feelings as moderately depressed or severely depressed?
I’d say moderately depressed, not severe. I can still get through my shift and talk to people, but inside I feel really sad and flat, like there’s this heavy, empty feeling in my chest.
Have you had to reduce your work hours or take any days off work because of how you've been feeling?

I haven’t really cut back my hours or taken full days off. I’m still going in, but I’m not as reliable with the details right now. I’ve had coworkers double-check my client documentation, and at home my wife’s been taking over some of the bills and scheduling.
Have you noticed any changes in how you interact with friends or family members since you started feeling this way?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think there’s been a big change. Maybe I’m a little quieter or less talkative than usual, but I’m still seeing my family and talking to people. Nothing really stands out to me.
Have you felt like withdrawing from friends or family because of how you've been feeling?
Not really, no. I mean, I might be a little less talkative sometimes, but I haven’t been avoiding my family or friends on purpose. I’m still around them.
Have you felt like you're pulling away from social interactions or activities with others because of your feelings?
I don’t think so. I’m still doing things with people when they come up. I might not be as chatty as usual, but I wouldn’t say I’m pulling away.
On most days, do you feel like you're able to find some pleasure in the things you're doing?
Yeah, I think so. I haven’t really noticed losing pleasure in things. Maybe some days I’m not as into it, but most days I can still enjoy what I’m doing.
Would you say that your depressive symptoms have caused significant impairment in your social or occupational functioning?

Yeah, somewhat. I wouldn’t say it’s completely stopping me, but it is affecting things. At work I’ve had to ask coworkers to double-check my client notes, and at home my wife’s been handling more of the bills and scheduling because I’m not as dependable with the details right now.
Have you had any days over the past month where you felt severely depressed?

Yeah, there have been days where it feels pretty heavy. I’ll wake up with this empty feeling in my chest, and I can still get through my shift and talk to people, but inside I feel really sad and flat.
